SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT

Pao Chia Section, Sp.Br.Station. File No.................... Date May 16, 1942.

SUBJECT: Alleged Forcible Collection of Contributions
to the Pao Chia System and Vigilance Corps

With reference to the attached note from
the Chairman of the Municipal Council and enclosed
circular on the subject of forcible collection of
contributions to the Pao Chia System or Vigilance
Corps, enquiries ascertained that any collection
solicited by members of the Pao Chia are made in
the form of loans which are being raised to cover
expenses in connection with the enforcement of the
Pao Chia System and the organization of the
Vigilance Corps. A decision to raise such loans
was made at a meeting of the Central Pao Chia District
Committee on May 8, 1942, when it was decided that
the Chiefs of Pao and Chia collect from Chinese
owned shops and firms loans towards the Pao Chia fund
in the following sums :- $100.00, $200.00, $500.00
and $1,000. The loan to be given voluntarily is
left to the discretion of each individual, on the
understanding that it will be refunded when funds
are received from the Municipal Council.

The collection of loans commenced on May 11,
1942 and the money thus raised are kept by the Chiefs
of Pao for the time being and temporary receipts
are issued by them. The money will be later handed
over to certain specified banks and then formal
receipts which will be signed by the Chief of the
District and members of the Finance Sub-Committee
will be issued. The receipts are now under preparation

firms of the decision to raise loans, copies of a

12th May 1942
4 p.m.

A circular is given to all firm managers at
the meeting held at the Moody office on 12th May 1942, requesting
all firms to contribute funds for the expenses of the "Pao Chia"
system.

" Central District of Shanghai International
Settlement.

It is now over 2 months since the organization of "Pao
Chia" system in this district under orders from the
Authorities. All expenses so far for the maintaining of
the system have been paid by the Chief "Pao Chia" officers.
The expenses for police whistles, police box and rain
coats etc are rather heavy and the Chief "Pao Chia" officers
are not in a position to bear such big amounts.
Although the S.M.C has passed a resolution to collect "Pao
Chia" tax to meet such expenses, the tax is not yet being
collected. We however cannot wait indefinitely for funds
to come from the S.M.C. while the costs of police whistles,
rain coats are getting higher & higher and the stocks of
such articles are getting scarce. We will not be able to
secure such articles at all if we wait any longer while the
shortage of such articles will certainly affect the peace
order of our district. At the Chief "Pao Chia" officers'
meeting on the 8th May 1942 it is decided that all firms are
requested to contribute from $ 100 to $1000 which will be
returned immediately when the S.M.C. is in a position to
defray such expenses. This decision is approved by the S.M
You are therefore requested to hand in your contributions
within 3 days from 11th May 1942 "

At today's meeting it was however resolved that instead of
voluntary contributions to be paid by each firm, the Chief
"Pao Chia" will advise us as to how much each firm has to
pay according to members and standing of the firm.

A second circular will come today or tomorrow.

1942年5月12日
下午4时

在1942年5月12日于马迪汽车公司 (Moody office) 举行的会议上，向所有公司经理发放了一份通函，要求各公司为“保甲”制度的费用提供资金。

“上海公共租界中央区。

在本区当局命令下组织‘保甲’制度至今已逾两个月。迄今为止，维持该制度的所有费用均由‘保甲’主要官员垫付。警哨、警亭和雨衣等物品的费用相当沉重，‘保甲’主要官员无力承担如此巨额费用。
虽然工部局 (S.M.C) 已通过决议征收‘保甲’税以支付此类费用，但该税尚未开始征收。然而，随着警哨、雨衣等物品成本日益高涨且库存日益稀缺，我们无法无限期等待工部局的资金到位。若再等待，我们将完全无法获得这些物品，而这些物品的短缺必将影响本区的治安秩序。在1942年5月8日的‘保甲’主要官员会议上，决定要求各公司捐助100元至1000元不等的款项，待工部局有能力支付此类费用时将立即归还。此决定已获工部局批准
因此，请阁下于1942年5月11日起3天内提交捐款”

然而在今天的会议上决议，不再由各公司支付自愿捐款，而是由‘保甲’负责人根据公司的成员数量和地位建议每家公司应支付的金额。

第二份通函将于今天或明天发出。

the Pao Chia system and Civilian Vigilance Corps to be taken
up in this district. In the past all expenses were advanced
by the various members of the Committee and the Heads of different
Pao. As a large sum of money is now required for the
installation of alarm bells, erection of additional watch
kiosks and the purchase of raincoats, the limited financial
resources of the Pao heads are unequal to meet this burden.
Though the Council intends to issue funds to us to cover our
expenses, the money required is still being raised and cannot
be released within a definite period. At the same time the
local stocks of materials for alarm bells and raincoats are
daily being depleted. Should purchase be further delayed, not
only will it be difficult for us to obtain the materials but
the peace and order of this district may be adversely affected.
It was therefore decided at a meeting of Pao heads held on
the 8th instant that the various wealthy merchants and
residents in this district should be requested to voluntarily
advance sums for the above-mentioned purposes. The amounts
to be advanced are of four classes, A, B, C and D, (A $1,000;
B. $500; C. $200; D $100.) The sums should be handed to the
heads of the various Pao and Chia' from whom provisional
receipts are to be obtained. The accumulated money shall be
sent to designated banks which will issue formal receipts to
be transmitted to the various merchants and residents to be
kept by them. When the Council has issued to us funds for the
Pao Chia expenses of this district the advances will be promptly
repaid. The three members of the Finance Committee of this

“保甲”制度；所需资金。

本区奉命实行保甲制度及民防自警团以来，已过去两个月。过去所有费用均由委员会各成员及各保长垫付。由于现在需要一大笔资金用于安装警报铃、增设守望岗亭及购买雨衣，各保长有限的财力不足以承担此负担。
虽然工部局打算向我们拨付资金以覆盖我们的开支，但所需资金仍在筹集中，无法在确定期限内发放。同时，当地警报铃和雨衣的材料库存日益减少。若采购进一步延迟，不仅我们将难以获得材料，本区的和平与秩序也可能受到不利影响。
因此，在本月8日举行的各保长会议上决定，请求本区各位富商及居民为上述目的自愿垫付款项。垫付款项分为四类，A、B、C和D类，（A类1,000元；B类500元；C类200元；D类100元。）款项应交给各保长和甲长，并从他们那里获取临时收据。累积的资金将送往指定银行，银行将出具正式收据，转交各位商户及居民保存。当工部局向我们拨付本区保甲费用资金时，垫付款将迅速偿还。本区财务委员会的三名成员

business or residing in this district. They are all generous
and public-spirited, and it may be presumed that they will not
lag behind others in rendering service to the community. As the
matter is of intimate concern to these merchants they should act
in a way to ensure success for our work. It must be pointed
out here that should the peace and order of this district not
be securely established, the wealth and properties of
individuals will have no protection. Commencing from 11th May
the sum to be advanced will be collected. It is hoped that
payments will be made promptly so that the requisite amount of
funds may be obtained within a short time. Our Central district
will then be a safe place for business and residence, as our
Civilian Vigilance Corps will attain full efficiency and no
terroristic incidents or blockades will occur in this locality.

关于强制征收保甲制度及守望队捐款的指控

参照随附的工部局主席便函及所附关于强制征收保甲制度或守望队捐款的通告，经查询查明，保甲成员所募集的任何款项均以贷款形式进行，旨在筹措与执行保甲制度及组织守望队相关的费用。中央保甲区委员会于1942年5月8日召开会议，决定筹集此类贷款，当时决定由保长和甲长向华人所有的商店和公司收取以下金额的保甲基金贷款：100.00元、200.00元、500.00元和1,000元。贷款遵循自愿原则，由个人自行决定，前提是当从工部局收到资金时将予以退还。

贷款征集工作于1942年5月11日开始，目前筹集的资金由保长暂时保管，并由他们出具临时收据。随后，资金将移交给指定的银行，届时将签发由区主任和财务小组委员会成员签署的正式收据。目前收据尚未准备就绪。

为了通知商店和公司业主关于筹集贷款的决定，准备了本报告主题的

circular notice, which is the subject of this
report, were prepared and distributed. Although
it was decided that the loans would be collected
from Chinese owned firms only, copies of the
circular notices have been distributed to foreign
firms, with the result that several complaints
have been received by the Police.

The collection is still in progress. It
is feared that the Chiefs of Pao and Chia might
resort to compulsory steps in the collection in
spite of the decision that the loans would be
voluntary.

According to the responsible Pao Chia officials
of the Central District, a loan of $70,000 has been
raised by the Chiefs of Pao at $2,000 each, and a
further loan of $50,000 has been obtained from five
banks in the District, making a total of $120,000.
More than $100,000 of this loan has already been
spent, but more money is required for the purchase
of rain coats, erection of more kiosks and the
installation of anti-terrorist alarm system.

During the course of the enquiries, it
has been learned that similar loans are being
collected in other Districts, which will be made
the subject of a further report.
